introduction: On this most holy night, the Church keeps vigil for the Lord's Resurrection. We begin in darkness with the new fire and the Easter candle, the sign of Christ our light. We listen to the story of salvation, from creation to the promises of the prophets. Tonight catechumens are baptized and receive the sacraments, and we all renew our baptismal promises. With the women at the tomb, we hear: Why do you seek the living among the dead?

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, on this night of light we rejoice with the newly baptized. Let us pray to the Father, who raised his Son from the dead.
intentions: For the Church throughout the world, keeping vigil tonight: that the light of the risen Christ may shine through her in every land. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the newly baptized and all who have been received into full communion: that they may walk in newness of life. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are perplexed and afraid, like the women at the tomb: that the good news of the Resurrection may fill them with hope. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who have died, especially those we have loved: that they may share in the Resurrection of Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves, who have renewed our baptismal promises: that we may live as people who are dead to sin and alive to God. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God of life, on this night you raised your Son from the dead and gave new life to your children in Baptism. Keep us faithful to the promises we have made, and fill us with Easter joy. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Why do you seek the living among the dead?
reflection.body:
The Easter Vigil tells the whole story of salvation in one night. We hear how God created all things and "saw everything that he had made, and, behold, it was very good." We hear Abraham's trust: "God will provide himself the lamb for a burnt offering, my son." We hear how Israel passed through the sea on dry ground, and how the prophets promised water for the thirsty and a new heart: "I will also give you a new heart, and I will put a new spirit within you."

All of this leads to the font. Paul tells us what Baptism means: "We were buried therefore with him through baptism into death, that just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, so we also might walk in newness of life."

Luke's Gospel takes us to the tomb at dawn. The women come with spices to anoint the body of Jesus. They find the stone rolled away and the tomb empty, and they are "greatly perplexed." Two men in dazzling clothes ask them a question for every age: "Why do you seek the living among the dead? He isn't here, but is risen."

They remind the women of what Jesus had told them, and "They remembered his words." The women run to tell the apostles, but their words "seemed to them to be nonsense." Only Peter gets up and runs to the tomb, and goes home "wondering what had happened." Faith in the Resurrection begins with women who remembered, and with wonder.

We too sometimes look for life in the wrong places, or among the dead things of our past. Tonight the Church announces that Christ is alive. When you renew your baptismal promises, say your yes with joy, and carry the light of the Easter candle into your home.
